reasons.plausibility: It is scientifically sound that a sulfur-based treatment can produce lubricious MoS2 in a Mo-containing high-entropy alloy, though questions remain about phase stability at high temperatures.
reasons.testability: The pin-on-disk comparison between treated and untreated samples across the specified temperature range provides a clear, decisive method to confirm or refute the predicted friction and wear reductions.
reasons.usefulness: Validating a robust, in-situ method to form MoS2 for self-lubrication could be highly valuable for extending the performance envelope of high-entropy alloys in moving components.
